newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight at 8.00/10 pct after choppy session.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight at 8.00/10 pct after choppy session.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate was quoted at 8.00/10 percent late on Thursday after a choppy session dominated by rumours of capital controls, dealers said.
The overnight traded between 7.0 and 9.0 percent, against 6.0 to 8.0 percent on Wednesday, they said.
"It was very choppy today as the market was a bit confused. There were a lot of rumours in the market," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
Among the rumours was that Bank Negara will be holding a meeting with bankers concerning the swaps, pushing swap rates higher across the board.
"Foreigners were covering their positions but I think it was more a precautionary move," one dealer said.
Banking sources said the central bank will be meeting the heads of selected banks on Friday to discuss routine foreign exchange activities of the banks.
"Bank Negara is calling a number of banks to talk about their activities and exposure in the forex market. This is quite routine," said a banking source.
Market players said Bank Negara was unlikely to impose any capital controls.

"The market is expected to hold its breath given the intensity of the rumours, even though we still hold onto the belief that there is no need for such drastic measures such as restriction on swaps," said research house MMS International.
Speculation over capital controls also lifted interbank rates from earlier levels.

The rates had earlier fallen in line with a drop in the overnight to as low as 6.0 percent on Wednesday after rumours that the statutory reserve requirement (SRR) may be cut due to the current tight liquidity situation.
"The rumour is still in the market though many are beginning to rule out the possibility of such a move," said one dealer.
Dealers said a cut in the SRR -- funds that must be placed interest free with the central bank -- would send a wrong signal to the market as monetary and consumption growth were still high.
Talk of the SRR cut followed Bank Negara's move in providing liquidity for the market via one-month money this week.
One- and two-week money were at 7.5/8.0 percent against 7.80/8.30 percent on Wednesday, dealers said.
One-month money was at 7.9/8.1 percent from 8.10/20, and three-month at 7.9/8.1 percent against 8.00/10.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were down across the board.
At 0900 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was down nine basis points to 92.06, or an implied yield of 7.94 percent.
The September contract was down six at 92.41, or 7.59 percent, and December was down five at 92.51, or 7.49 percent.
